core: Occupancy rate = rooms sold / rooms available (a percentage of capacity used)
Average Daily Rate (ADR) = rooms revenue / rooms sold (average price per occupied room)
Revenue Per Available Room (RevPAR) = rooms revenue / rooms available
The RevPAR identity: RevPAR = ADR x occupancy, demonstrated numerically

Rate fences (advance purchase, non-refundable, length-of-stay) as conditions attached to lower rates
The occupancy-versus-ADR trade-off: chasing 100% occupancy by discounting can lower RevPAR

claims.claim: Occupancy rate is the percentage of available rooms that are sold over a given period, computed as rooms sold divided by rooms available.
Average Daily Rate (ADR) is the average revenue earned per occupied room, calculated by dividing total rooms revenue by the number of rooms sold; complimentary and house-use rooms are excluded.
RevPAR (Revenue Per Available Room) equals total rooms revenue divided by the number of available rooms, and equivalently equals ADR multiplied by the occupancy rate.

RevPAR gives a more complete picture of rooms performance than ADR or occupancy alone because it accounts for unsold rooms; selling rooms at lower rates just to boost occupancy can reduce overall revenue.

The rack rate is the officially published, highest standard rate for a room type; hotels rarely charge it and use it as a benchmark, while the Best Available Rate (BAR) is the lowest unrestricted publicly available rate for a date.
Rate fences are conditions attached to a discounted rate that a guest must meet to qualify, such as advance-purchase cutoffs, non-refundable payment, and minimum or maximum length of stay.

Advance-purchase rates offer a discount off BAR in exchange for booking days-to-months ahead and are typically non-refundable, shifting cancellation risk to the guest and guaranteeing the hotel revenue.
GOPPAR (gross operating profit per available room) is an industry-standard KPI that, unlike RevPAR, subtracts operating expenses before dividing by available rooms.

Discounted and negotiated rates arise from segmented pricing, in which the same room is sold at different rates to different market segments such as government, corporate partners, and loyalty members.
Lodging managers monitor room occupancy and rates and are responsible for the property's revenue performance as part of their standard duties.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether 'rooms available' should count out-of-order (temporarily unusable) rooms in occupancy and RevPAR denominators.
positions: Some operators exclude rooms out of order for maintenance from available inventory, raising measured occupancy.
Standardized benchmarking generally uses total physical rooms so figures compare across properties and dates.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses total physical rooms as the denominator for clarity and consistency, and notes that definitions of 'available' can vary; it does not rely on any proprietary benchmark convention.
